|-
|[[Subjunctive mood|Subjunctive]]
|Event is considered unlikely (mainly used in dependent clauses).
|"If I loved you...", "May I love you"
|ganai la'anai ... gi ...
ganai ju'onai ... gi
|doesn't take into account unlikeliness and assertion of not possibly becoming real thus not being different from Conditional (add '''to na ku da'i toi'''?)
|[[English language|English]]<nowiki> | </nowiki>[[Latin language|Latin]] &#124; [[German Language|German]] &#124; [[Romance languages]] &#124; [[Vedic Sanskrit]] &#124; [[Proto-Indo-European language|Proto-Indo-European]] &#124; [[Hindi]]
|-
|[[Conditional mood|Conditional]]
|Event depends upon another condition.
|"I would love you"
|da'i
ganai ... gi
|
|[[English language|English]] &#124; [[German language|German]] &#124; [[Romance languages]] &#124; [[Icelandic language|Icelandic]] &#124; [[Irish language|Irish]] &#124; [[Hindi]] &#124; [[Finnish language|Finnish]] &#124; [[Hungarian language|Hungarian]]
|-
|[[Optative mood|Optative]]
|Event is hoped,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Optative Mood|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/optative-mood|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref> expected, or awaited.
|"May I be loved!"
|.a'o
ba'a
.au
|doesn't relay expectation
|[[Albanian language|Albanian]] &#124; [[Ancient Greek]] &#124; [[Sanskrit]] &#124; [[Avestan]] &#124; [[Proto-Indo-European language|Proto-Indo-European]]
|-
|[[Jussive mood|Jussive]]
|Event is pleaded, implored or asked.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Jussive Mood|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/jussive-mood|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref>
|"Everyone should be loved"
|.ei
|
|[[Arabic language|Arabic]] &#124; [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] &#124; [[Esperanto]]
|-
|[[Potential mood|Potential]]
|Event is probable or considered likely
|"She probably loves me"
|la'a
|
|[[Finnish language|Finnish]] &#124; [[Japanese language|Japanese]] &#124; [[Sanskrit]] &#124; [[Sami languages]] &#124; [[Proto-Indo-European language|Proto-Indo-European]]
|-
|[[Imperative mood|Imperative]] and Prohibitive
|Event is directly ordered or requested by the speaker.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Imperative Mood|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/imperative-mood|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref> Prohibitive is the negation of an imperative statement, i.e., the speaker prohibits an event (orders to it not occur).<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Prohibitive Mood|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/prohibitive-mood|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref>
|"Love me!", "Do not love me"
|.e'i (BPFK)
|The CLL doesn't have an example of '''.e'i'''
|[[English language|English]]<ref name=":1" /> &#124; [[Seri language|Seri]] &#124; [[Latin Language|Latin]] &#124; [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]] (Portuguese has distinct Imperative and Prohibitive moods)  &#124; [[Finnish language|Finnish]] &#124; [[Hungarian language|Hungarian]]
|-
|[[Desiderative mood|Desiderative]]
|Event is desired/wished by a participant in the state of affairs referred to in the utterance<ref>{{Cite web|title=WALS Online - Chapter The Optative|url=https://wals.info/chapter/73#:~:text=3.2.&text=Both%20categories%20involve%20the%20expression,referred%20to%20in%20the%20utterance.|access-date=2021-05-11|website=wals.info}}</ref>
|"I wish she loved me."
|.au
|
|[[Sanskrit]] &#124; [[Japanese language|Japanese]] &#124; [[Proto-Indo-European language|Proto-Indo-European]]
|-
|[[Dubitative mood|Dubitative]]
|Event is uncertain, doubtful, dubious.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Dubitative Mood|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/dubitative-mood|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref>
|"I think she loves me."
|ju'ocu'i
|The CLL uses '''ju'o''' and '''la'a''' scales for hypothetical worlds
|[[Ojibwe language|Ojibwe]]<ref name=":2" /> &#124; [[Turkish language|Turkish]]
|-
|[[Hypothetical mood|Hypothetical]]
|Event is hypothetical, or it is [[Counterfactual conditional|counterfactual]], but possible.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Hypothetical Mood|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/hypothetical-mood|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref>
|"I might love you [if...]"
|da'i
|
|[[Russian language|Russian]] &#124; [[Lakota language|Lakota]]<ref name=":3" />
|-
|[[Presumptive mood|Presumptive]]
|Event is assumed, presupposed by the speaker
|There is no exact English example, although it could be translated as: "[Even if] he loves you [...]"
|
|no translation?
|[[Romanian language|Romanian]] &#124; [[Hindi]] &#124; [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]] &#124; [[Gujarati language|Gujarati]]
|-
|[[Permissive mood|Permissive]]
|Event is permitted by the speaker.<ref>{{cite web|editor1-last=Loos|editor1-first=Eugene E.|editor2-last=Anderson|editor2-first=Susan|editor3-last=Day|editor3-first=Dwight H. Jr.|editor4-last=Jordan|editor4-first=Paul C.|editor5-last=Wingate|editor5-first=J. Douglas|title=What is permissive mood?|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/permissive-mood|access-date=2009-12-28|work=Glossary of linguistic terms|publisher=SIL International}}</ref>
|"You may [not] love me..."
|.e'a
|
|[[Lithuanian language|Lithuanian]] (as a form of optative mood)
|-
|[[Mirative|Admirative]]
|Event is surprising or amazing (literally or in irony or sarcasm).
|"Wow! She loves me!"
|u'e, ue
|
|[[Turkish language|Turkish]] &#124; [[Bulgarian language|Bulgarian]] &#124; [[Macedonian language|Macedonian]] &#124; [[Albanian language|Albanian]] &#124; [[Megleno-Romanian language|Megleno-Romanian]]
|-
|[[Hortative]]
|Event is exhorted, implored, insisted or encouraged by speaker.
|"Let us love!"
|.e'ei
|
|[[Latin language|Latin]] (as a form of jussive) &#124; [[Greek Language|Greek]] (as a form of the subjunctive)<ref>{{cite book |last1=Smyth |first1=Herbert |title=Greek Grammar |date=1984 |publisher=Harvard University Press |location=Cambridge |isbn=0-674-36250-0 |pages=403–404 (§1797–1799)}}</ref> &#124; [[Hindi]]
|-
|{{visanc|Eventive|Eventive mood}}
|Event is likely but depends upon a condition. It is a combination of the potential and the conditional moods.
|"I would probably love you [if...]"
|ganai ... gi la'a ...
|
|[[Finnish language|Finnish]] (in the epic poem [[Kalevala]]) &#124; [[Estonian language|Estonian]], in some dialects
|-
|Precative
|Event is requested by the speaker.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Precative Mood|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/precative-mood|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref>
|"Will you love me?"
|.e'o
|
|
|-
|[[Volitive modality|Volitive]]
|Event is desired, wished or feared by the speaker.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-12-03|title=Volitive Modality|url=https://glossary.sil.org/term/volitive-modality|access-date=2020-08-12|website=SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms|language=en}}</ref>
|"Would that you loved me!" / "God forbid [that] you love me!"
|.au
|
|
|-
|[[Inferential mood|Inferential]]
|Event is nonwitnessed, and not confirmed.
|There is no exact English example, although it could be translated as: "She is said to love me"
|ti'e
|?
|[[Turkish language|Turkish]] &#124; [[Bulgarian language|Bulgarian]] (Inferential mood is called "renarrative mood") &#124; [[Estonian language|Estonian]] (It is called "oblique mood")
|-
|[[Necessitative]]
|Event is necessary, or it is both desired and encouraged. It is a combination of hortative and jussive.
|
|.ei .e'ei
|
|[[Armenian language|Armenian]] &#124; [[Turkish language|Turkish]]
|-
|[[Interrogative mood|Interrogative]]
|Event is asked or questioned by the speaker
|"Does she love me?"
|xu
|
|[[Welsh language|Welsh]] &#124; [[Nenets language|Nenets]]
|}
